ei.subject: 영어1
ei.title: From a Kid to a Champion

fullPassage:
My name is Bliksem, which means "lightning." My parents named me this because they wanted me to be faster than anyone else. Born in the Netherlands, a country with more bicycles than people, I learned to ride a bike almost as soon as I could walk. I loved feeling the breeze in my hair. When I was eleven, a junior bicycle race was held in our small town. I entered the race as the youngest rider. Before the race started, I looked around the crowd, and I couldn't believe my eyes! My hero, Gabriel Martinez, the cycling world champion, was standing there! I ran over and asked, "You're Gabriel Martinez, right? Can I have your autograph?" He smiled and said, "If you win, you can." Excited by what he said, I pedaled harder than ever. I came in first and Gabriel was waiting at the finish line. As promised, he handed me his autograph saying, "You outran the others by two laps! You're a real racer, kid!"

Since then, Gabriel has been my mentor. When I turned nineteen, he brought me into his professional team, where only the most skilled and passionate cyclists came together. I felt small and insignificant. I could sprint the fastest on flat courses, but I always fell behind in mountain races. The Netherlands is mostly flat, so I had rarely cycled up steep slopes before. Gabriel was from Bogotá, Colombia, which is high up in the Andes. He had a lot of experience in riding on hills and mountains, so he was always the first to arrive at the top. He would say, "Riding uphill is painful, but the view at the top is fantastic. Never stop pedaling, kid."

Motivated by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated eagerly in all the training courses, especially the uphill ones. Soon after, my efforts finally paid off in one of the mountain courses. As a domestique, who supports the leader and the team during a cycling race, I was riding in front of Gabriel to shield him from the headwind. Our team was far ahead of the others. Everything was going perfectly until I crashed due to a crack in the road. All four of us fell in the crash, and the other teams passed us by. I was just slightly wounded, but Gabriel's injury was more serious. He urged me to continue on his behalf. But there were a couple of more steep slopes ahead, and I doubted we had a chance. Gabriel read my mind and yelled, "Remember the view at the top. Never stop pedaling whatever it takes, kid. Now go!"

Pedaling with all my strength, I finished second in that race, but I felt a sense of guilt for my fellow team members. I should have been more careful. If I had not crashed, Gabriel would have come in first place, and our team would have won. Surprisingly, Gabriel gave me a gentle hug and said, "I knew you could do it. I'm so proud of you!"

For several years, I assisted Gabriel in races as a domestique. As we cycled together, our team's results flourished. When the time came for his retirement, Gabriel asked the members if I could lead the team in his final race. He said he could no longer ride faster than me in the last sprint to the finish line and insisted that I ought to be the team leader. I was deeply touched and felt a burden on my shoulders. I was determined to make him proud.

Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250 km race famed for its cobblestone sections. These bumpy roads were a true test of endurance, talent, and mental power for every cyclist. As the race started, I focused on my strategy and my desire to win. However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue. Gabriel offered me his bike without hesitation, saying, "I remember your finishing the race two laps ahead of everyone when I first met you. Never stop pedaling, kid. I'll catch up." The rest of the members urged me on and we continued, pushing ourselves to our limits. When there were only 10 km left in the race, Gabriel caught up with us on a new bicycle. He cut in front of me and said, "Save your energy now for the final sprint. We'll help you to the finish line."

Our speed increased as we approached the finish line, and my teammates worked hard to support me. When the finish line came into view, I began my final sprint with a rush of adrenaline, and our rivals were right on my tail, fighting for the same victory. Finally, I crossed the finish line ahead of my competitors by a nose.

The crowd roared tremendously. They focused on me since I was the first to cross the finish line. As I stood on the podium holding the trophy high, I felt like the glory should go to Gabriel. However, when I looked over, I could see the pride in his eyes.

He said, "That trophy is yours, Captain." It was the first time he had not addressed me as "kid." My teammates approached me as tears welled up in my eyes, saying, "We're counting on you, Captain."

questions.passage: My name is Bliksem, which means "lightning." My parents named me this because they wanted me to be faster than anyone else. Born in the Netherlands, a country with more bicycles than people, I ①<u>learned</u> to ride a bike almost as soon as I could walk. I loved ②<u>feeling</u> the breeze in my hair. When I was eleven, a junior bicycle race was ③<u>held</u> in our small town. I entered the race as the ④<u>young</u> rider.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ young → youngest: 가장 어린 선수로 참가했으므로 최상급이 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ young → youngest: 'as the youngest rider'가 원문. 최상급 필요.
❌ ① learned: 과거시제 적절.
❌ ② feeling: love + 동명사 패턴 적절.
❌ ③ held: 수동태(was held) 적절.
det.tip: love/enjoy/finish + -ing(동명사). the + 최상급 + 명사 = 가장 ~한.

questions.passage: Since then, Gabriel has been my mentor. When I turned nineteen, he brought me into his professional team, ①<u>where</u> only the most skilled and passionate cyclists came together. I felt small and insignificant. I could sprint the fastest on flat courses, but I always fell behind in mountain races. The Netherlands is mostly flat, so I had ②<u>rarely</u> cycled up steep slopes before. Gabriel was from Bogotá, Colombia, ③<u>which</u> is high up in the Andes. He had a lot of experience in ④<u>ride</u> on hills and mountains.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ ride → riding: 전치사 in 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ ride → riding: 'experience in riding'이 원문. 전치사 + 동명사.
❌ ① where: 선행사 team(장소) → 관계부사 where 적절.
❌ ② rarely: 부사(거의 ~않다) 적절.
❌ ③ which: 선행사 Colombia(사물/장소 주격) → which 적절.
det.tip: 전치사(in, of, at, for) + 동명사(-ing). 'experience in + -ing' = ~한 경험.

questions.passage: Motivated by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated eagerly in all the training courses. As a domestique, ①<u>who</u> supports the leader and the team during a cycling race, I was riding in front of Gabriel to shield him from the headwind. Everything was going perfectly until I ②<u>crashed</u> due to a crack in the road. All four of us fell in the crash, and the other teams ③<u>passed</u> us by. Gabriel's injury was more serious. He urged me ④<u>continuing</u> on his behalf.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ continuing → to continue: urge는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ continuing → to continue: 'urge + 목적어 + to-V' 구문.
❌ ① who: 선행사 domestique(사람) → 주격 관계대명사 적절.
❌ ② crashed: 과거시제 적절.
❌ ③ passed: 과거시제, 'pass ~ by' = ~을 지나치다.
det.tip: urge/encourage/advise/persuade + 목적어 + to-V. 5형식 to부정사 목적격보어.

questions.passage: Pedaling with all my strength, I finished second in that race, but I felt a sense of guilt for my fellow team members. I should have been more careful. If I ①<u>had not crashed</u>, Gabriel ②<u>would have come</u> in first place, and our team would have won. Surprisingly, Gabriel gave me a gentle hug and said, "I ③<u>knew</u> you could do it. I'm so ④<u>proudly</u> of you!"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ proudly → proud: be동사(am) 뒤에는 보어로 형용사가 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ proudly(부사) → proud(형용사): 'I'm so proud of you'가 원문. be + 형용사.
❌ ① had not crashed: 가정법 과거완료 if절 적절.
❌ ② would have come: 가정법 과거완료 주절 적절.
❌ ③ knew: 과거시제 직접화법 적절.
det.tip: be + 형용사(보어). proud(형용사) vs. proudly(부사). 가정법 과거완료: If + had p.p., would have p.p.

questions.passage: For several years, I assisted Gabriel in races as a domestique. As we cycled together, our team's results flourished. When the time came for his retirement, Gabriel asked the members if I could lead the team in his final race. He said he could no longer ride faster than me in the last sprint to the finish line and __________ that I ought to be the team leader.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 내가 팀 리더가 되어야 한다고 주장했다(insisted).
det.analysis:
✅ ① insisted(주장하다): 더 이상 나보다 빠르지 않으니 리더가 되어야 한다는 주장.
❌ ② denied(부인하다): 리더 역할을 추천하는 맥락과 반대.
❌ ③ doubted(의심하다): 확신 있게 말하는 맥락.
❌ ④ regretted(후회하다): 문맥 불일치.
det.tip: insist (that) + S + (should) V = ~해야 한다고 주장하다.

questions.passage: Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250 km race ①<u>famed</u> for its cobblestone sections. These bumpy roads were a true test of endurance, talent, and mental power for every cyclist. As the race started, I focused on my strategy and my desire to win. However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue. Gabriel offered me his bike without ②<u>hesitation</u>. The rest of the members urged me on and we continued, pushing ourselves to our ③<u>limits</u>. When there were only 10 km left in the race, Gabriel caught up with us on a new bicycle. He cut in front of me and said, "Save your energy now for the final ④<u>retreat</u>."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ retreat(후퇴) → sprint(전력질주): 결승선을 향한 마지막 전력질주를 위해 에너지를 아끼라는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ retreat → sprint: '결승선 질주'가 아니라 '후퇴'는 경주 맥락과 모순.
❌ ① famed(유명한): 파리-루베가 자갈 구간으로 유명.
❌ ② hesitation(망설임): 주저 없이 자전거를 내밈.
❌ ③ limits(극한): 극한까지 밀어붙이며 계속함.
det.tip: sprint(전력질주) ↔ retreat(후퇴). 'the final sprint' = 마지막 전력질주.

questions.passage: My name is Bliksem, which means "lightning." My parents named me this because they wanted me to be faster than anyone else. Born in the Netherlands, a country with more bicycles than people, I learned to ride a bike almost as soon as I could walk.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"Bliksem의 이름은 '번개'라는 뜻이며, 네덜란드에서 태어났다."

det.korean: Bliksem = lightning(번개), Born in the Netherlands.
det.analysis: ✅ T: '번개'라는 뜻 + 네덜란드 출생 모두 원문 일치.
det.tip: the Netherlands = 네덜란드. Bliksem은 네덜란드어로 '번개'.

questions.passage: Since then, Gabriel has been my mentor. When I turned nineteen, he brought me into his professional team. I could sprint the fastest on flat courses, but I always fell behind in mountain races. The Netherlands is mostly flat, so I had rarely cycled up steep slopes before. Gabriel was from Bogotá, Colombia, which is high up in the Andes.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"Bliksem은 평지에서는 빨랐지만, 산악 경주에서는 Gabriel보다 앞섰다."

det.korean: 평지에서 가장 빨랐지만, 산악 경주에서는 항상 뒤처졌다(fell behind).
det.analysis: ✅ F: 'always fell behind in mountain races' = 산악에서 항상 뒤처짐. '앞섰다'는 반대.
det.tip: fall behind = 뒤처지다 ↔ get ahead = 앞서다.

questions.passage: Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250 km race famed for its cobblestone sections. These bumpy roads were a true test of endurance, talent, and mental power for every cyclist. However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue. Gabriel offered me his bike without hesitation.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"Paris-Roubaix 경주에서 Bliksem의 타이어가 펑크 나자, Gabriel은 자신의 자전거를 주저 없이 내주었다."

det.korean: 자갈길에서 타이어 펑크(flat tire) → Gabriel이 주저 없이(without hesitation) 자전거를 내줌.
det.analysis: ✅ T: flat tire + Gabriel offered his bike without hesitation 모두 원문 일치.
det.tip: flat tire = 타이어 펑크. without hesitation = 주저 없이.

questions.passage: Motivated by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated eagerly in all the training courses, especially the uphill ones. Soon after, my efforts finally paid off in one of the mountain courses. As a domestique, who supports the leader and the team during a cycling race, I was riding in front of Gabriel to __________ him from the headwind. Our team was far ahead of the others.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 맞바람으로부터 그를 보호하기(shield) 위해 앞에서 달렸다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ shield(보호하다): domestique가 리더 앞에서 바람을 막아줌.
❌ ① expose(노출시키다): shield의 반의어.
❌ ② separate(분리하다): 함께 달리고 있으므로 불일치.
❌ ④ distract(산만하게 하다): 바람과 무관.
det.tip: shield ~ from = ~로부터 보호하다. domestique = 팀 보조 선수.

questions.passage: Our speed increased as we approached the finish line, and my teammates worked hard to support me. When the finish line came into view, I began my final sprint with a rush of adrenaline, and our rivals were right on my tail, fighting for the same victory. Finally, I crossed the finish line ahead of my competitors __________. The crowd roared tremendously.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 경쟁자를 근소한 차이로(by a nose) 앞서 결승선 통과.
det.analysis:
✅ ② by a nose(근소한 차이로): 'right on my tail'(바로 뒤를 쫓음) → 아슬아슬한 승리.
❌ ① by miles(큰 차이로): 바로 뒤를 쫓았으므로 모순.
❌ ③ with ease(쉽게): 라이벌이 바로 뒤를 쫓는 상황.
❌ ④ after hesitating(망설인 후): 전력 질주했으므로 불일치.
det.tip: by a nose = 아슬아슬하게. right on my tail = 바로 뒤를 쫓다.

questions.passage: When I was eleven, a junior bicycle race was held in our small town. I entered the race as the youngest rider. Before the race started, I looked around the crowd, and I couldn't believe my eyes! My hero, Gabriel Martinez, the cycling world champion, was standing there! I ran over and asked, "You're Gabriel Martinez, right? Can I have your autograph?" He smiled and said, "If you win, you can." Excited by what he said, I pedaled harder than ever. I came in first and Gabriel was waiting at the finish line.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Bliksem은 열세 살에 첫 자전거 대회에 참가했다.
Gabriel은 경주 전에 Bliksem에게 사인을 해주었다.
Gabriel은 Bliksem이 우승하면 사인을 해주겠다고 했다.

det.korean: Gabriel: "네가 이기면(If you win), 사인 해줄게."
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 우승 조건 사인: 'If you win, you can' 원문 일치.
❌ ① 열세 살: eleven(열한 살)이 원문.
❌ ② 경주 전 사인: 우승 후에 사인을 받음.
❌ ③ 2등: came in first(1등).
det.tip: come in first = 1등하다. autograph = (유명인의) 사인.

questions.passage: For several years, I assisted Gabriel in races as a domestique. As we cycled together, our team's results flourished. When the time came for his retirement, Gabriel asked the members if I could lead the team in his final race. He said he could no longer ride faster than me in the last sprint to the finish line and insisted that I ought to be the team leader. I was deeply touched and felt a burden on my shoulders. I was determined to make him proud.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: Gabriel은 마지막 질주에서 더 이상 Bliksem보다 빠르지 않다고 했다.
Bliksem은 팀 리더 제안을 받고 안도감을 느꼈다.
Gabriel은 은퇴 경기에서 Bliksem에게 팀을 이끌어 달라고 했다.

det.korean: ③ 안도감 → 부담(burden): 'felt a burden on my shoulders' = 어깨에 부담을 느꼈다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 불일치: relief(안도감)가 아닌 burden(부담)이 원문.
❌ ① 일치: 'assisted Gabriel as a domestique'.
❌ ② 일치: 'asked if I could lead the team in his final race'.
❌ ④ 일치: 'could no longer ride faster than me'.
det.tip: burden(부담) ↔ relief(안도감). 'felt a burden on my shoulders' = 책임감에 부담을 느끼다.

questions.passage: He said, "That trophy is yours, Captain." It was the first time he had not addressed me as "kid." My teammates approached me ①<u>as</u> tears welled up in ②<u>my</u> eyes, ③<u>say</u>, "We're counting ④<u>on</u> you, Captain."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ say → saying: 동시동작의 분사구문. teammates가 다가오며 '말하는' 동시동작.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ say → saying: 주어(teammates)가 접근하면서 '말하는' 동시동작 → 현재분사.
❌ ① as: 접속사(~할 때) 적절.
❌ ② my: 소유격 적절.
❌ ④ on: 'count on' = ~을 믿다, 전치사 on 적절.
det.tip: 분사구문(동시동작): 주절 + , + V-ing. 'approached me, saying ~' = 다가오며 ~라고 말했다.

Since then, Gabriel has been my mentor. When I turned nineteen, he brought me into his professional team, where only the most skilled and passionate cyclists came together. I felt small and insignificant. I could sprint the fastest on flat courses, but I always __________ in mountain races. The Netherlands is mostly flat, so I had rarely cycled up steep slopes before. Gabriel was from Bogotá, Colombia, which is high up in the Andes. He had a lot of experience in riding on hills and mountains, so he was always the first to arrive at the top. He would say, "Riding uphill is painful, but the view at the top is fantastic.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"Bliksem은 평지에서는 가장 빠르게 달릴 수 있었지만, 산악 경주에서는 항상 __________."

det.korean: 산악 경주에서 항상 뒤처졌다(fell behind).
det.analysis: 원문: 'I always fell behind in mountain races.' → '뒤처졌다'에 해당하는 표현 = fell behind.
det.tip: fall behind = 뒤처지다. fall-fell-fallen.

questions.passage: Gabriel was from Bogotá, Colombia, which is high up in the Andes. He had a lot of experience in riding on hills and mountains, so he was always the first __________ (arrive) at the top. He would say, "Riding uphill is painful, but the view at the top is fantastic."
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 그는 항상 정상에 도착하는(to arrive) 첫 번째 사람이었다.
det.analysis: the first/last/only + to-V 구문. 서수/최상급 뒤에 to부정사가 온다.
det.tip: the first/second/last/only + to-V(to부정사): '~하는 첫 번째/마지막/유일한'.

questions.passage: I was deeply touched and felt a burden on my shoulders. __________. Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250 km race famed for its cobblestone sections.
questions.stem:
다음 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)

questions.passage: Since then, Gabriel has been my mentor. When I turned nineteen, he brought me into his professional team, where only the most skilled and passionate cyclists came together. I felt small and insignificant. I could sprint the fastest on flat courses, but I always fell behind in mountain races. Gabriel was from Bogotá, Colombia, which is high up in the Andes. He would say, "Riding uphill is painful, but the view at the top is fantastic. Never stop pedaling, kid." Motivated by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated eagerly in all the training courses, especially the uphill ones. Soon after, my efforts finally paid off in one of the mountain courses.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Gabriel의 격려(encouragement)에 힘입어 훈련에 매진하고 노력이 결실을 맺었다(paid off).
det.analysis:
✅ ② 멘토의 격려와 노력: Gabriel의 격려 → 훈련 참여 → 성과.
❌ ① 무용함: 노력이 결실을 맺었으므로 반대.
❌ ③ 위험성: 산악 자전거의 위험이 아닌 훈련과 성장.
❌ ④ 경쟁: 팀 간 경쟁이 아닌 개인 성장에 초점.
det.tip: 주제 = 글의 핵심 메시지. 멘토 격려 + 노력 → 성장이 핵심.

questions.passage: Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250 km race famed for its cobblestone sections. However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue. Gabriel offered me his bike without hesitation. When there were only 10 km left, Gabriel caught up with us on a new bicycle. He cut in front of me and said, "Save your energy now for the final sprint." Our speed increased as we approached the finish line, and my teammates worked hard to support me. Finally, I crossed the finish line ahead of my competitors by a nose.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸에 가장 적절한 것은?

"Paris-Roubaix 경주에서 타이어 펑크라는 위기에도 불구하고, Gabriel과 팀원들의 __________ 덕분에 Bliksem이 우승할 수 있었다."

det.korean: 타이어 펑크 위기 → Gabriel 자전거 제공 + 팀원 지원 → 헌신적인 지원 덕에 우승.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 헌신적인 지원: 자전거 제공, 에너지 아끼게 도움, 결승선까지 지원.
❌ ② 무관심한 태도: 적극적 도움과 반대.
❌ ③ 비판적 조언: 격려와 지원이지 비판 아님.
❌ ④ 일방적 명령: 함께 달리며 도운 것이지 명령이 아님.
det.tip: 요약 = 핵심만 추출. 위기(펑크) + 도움(팀워크) + 결과(우승).
